rows.title: THE TRUMPETER
rows.description: THEATRE DRAMA THE TRUMPETER Get Tickets Presented by: Alliance for New Music-Theatre in partnership with Ukraine House and United Help Ukraine Written by Inna Goncharova | English Translation by John Farndon Directed by János Szász Alliance for New Music-Theatre’s production of The Trumpeter returns to Dupont Underground for an immersive experience! Following a successful run garnering critical acclaim and a Helen Hayes Recommendation, this powerful production returns to the bunker-like tunnels of Dupont Underground for 13 performances. Staged in the tunnel, Inna Goncharova’s play captures the siege and bombing of Mariupol during the first year of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Directed by Hungarian director János Szász, the show features DC actors Michael Kevin Darnall and Lise Bruneau, enriched by trumpeter Kevin McKee and a male chorus of Ukrainian singers led by Ruslan Bondar. Audiences will also experience complementary photo exhibits curated by Ukraine House and United Help Ukraine in the venue prior to the performance. rows.title: Desi Alexander
rows.description: Baltimore native Desi Alexander is a high-energy stand-up comedian, writer, and director known for his fearless storytelling and razor-sharp wit. What started as teaching by day and performing by night quickly turned into a full-time calling — a destiny foreshadowed by the name his late father gave him, inspired by a classic bit from Eddie Murphy’s Delirious. With an engaged following of more than 500,000 fans worldwide, Desi has built a loyal audience drawn to his raw honesty, animated delivery, and relatable edge. His upcoming comedy special Stress Signal expands on the high-energy style that’s made him a crowd favorite across the country. Beyond the stage, Desi is the creative force behind Redeye Valley Films. His action film Flood is streaming on Tubi, while his acclaimed projects The Realtor (Amazon) and Check Please (Tubi) showcase his range as a writer and director. For the past eight years, Desi has toured and written alongside Jess Hilarious and has shared the stage with comedy heavyweights including Kevin Hart, Chris Tucker, Tommy Davidson, Bruce Bruce, Paul Mooney and many other countless legends. Now headlining his nationwide Stress Signal tour, Desi Alexander brings explosive energy, sharp perspective, and unforgettable laughs to stages across the country. rows.title: Sophia Bush
rows.description: Sophia Bush has always understood the power of stories. She’s seen it in the connection millions of viewers have had to the women she’s played on-screen—Dr. Sam Griffith on “Good Sam” and Dr. Cass Beckman on “Grey’s Anatomy,” Detective Erin Lindsay on “Chicago P.D.,” and the iconic Brooke Davis on “One Tree Hill.” She’s seen it in her activism, where speaking truth to inequality and power has prompted real change. And she’s seen it in her personal life, when her experiences and opinions have been distorted to drive clicks and create drama. In And I Will Tell You Mine, Bush shares stories about what has most shaped her: her childhood in Los Angeles, the unexpected road from journalism student to actor, navigating Hollywood and fighting for her character’s integrity, and the realities of marriage and divorce. She also offers sides of herself not often seen: the lifelong learner, the friend, the adventurer. And I Will Tell You Mine is an account of becoming, un-becoming, and becoming again to return home to our truest selves. Bush will be in conversation with Aaron Parnas, an independent journalist, political commentator, and attorney. This service will be ASL-interpreted. To sit in the interpreted section or to access the interpreted feed virtually, contact Amanda.

He is joined on the Bossa stage every Friday night by an ebullient and first-class roster of musicians, sure to have you breaking a sweat on the dance floor with salsa, bachata, merengue, and more. rows.title: ¡Latin Night with Tumbao!

books.title: Algorithm of the Night
books.description: A. S. Hamrah returns with an extraordinary collection of his best film writing for n+1, The Baffler, The New York Review of Books, the Criterion Collection, and other publications. Algorithm of the Night assembles Hamrah's essays on films and filmmakers and his inimitable, aphoristic reviews--a body of work that, taken together, presents a powerful alternative to a culture mired in publicity and stale convention. A journey through the overlapping dystopias of the Trump years, the Covid years, and the Trump years, Algorithm of the Night attends with remarkable style and precision to a film industry in self-imposed crisis, a chronicle of failures and occasional miracles from AI to The Zone of Interest. Against the tides of ignorance and solipsism, Algorithm of the Night is film criticism as literature and--perhaps--prophecy.

rows.title: An Afternoon with Rachel Levitin
rows.description: Imagine this - it’s Sunday afternoon and there’s nowhere you have to be. All that’s left is to sit back, relax, and decompress; leaving the heaviness of the modern world behind. Instead, you opt for a brief retreat to a sweet, experiential solace that is the matinee showing of a revered life-long artist’s latest creative connection with her audience. Join this interactive, conversational, live music concert curated and performed by singer-songwriter and executive producer Rachel Levitin. Hosted and guided by award-winning vocalist Jarreau Williams. “An Afternoon with Rachel Levitin” is a milestone event celebrating a wide variety of Rachel’s accomplishments such as: 30 years as a student of music, 27 as a songwriter, 21 since the release of her debut album “Come As You Are,” 20 living in the District of Columbia, 10 since the release of her unanimous fan-favorite “Get Back Up,” and 6 since production began on her 2024 album “Witty Banter,” all culminating to the world premiere of Rachel’s newest song, “Eulogy,” written, recorded, and performed in loving memory of her late grandfather, the beloved Edwin H. Levitin, who passed away in February 2026. Growing up in the city of Chicago, she didn't initially aspire to be a pop-rock recording artist, but an eclectic love of jazz, early aughts radio hits, and expressive ambition led Rachel Levitin to pick up her first guitar as a tween. As the ordinary and extraordinary traumas of early adulthood crashed down, Levitin channeled her grief, optimism, and growth into her lyrics. A move to DC in 2005 introduced her to the Washington-area music scene, where she quickly established a reputation for herself as a confident performer and a stalwart supporter of her peers. Her debut EP, "Nearly Broken" was released in 2015 and was followed by a string of singles, including 2021's "Off My Mind", which showcased Levitin's ability to write an unforgettable hook. In an age when wispy cynicism is en vogue, Levitin's earnest, raw lyricism sets her apart from the crowd. Her music combines the endorphin rushes of early aughts hits with the emotional vulnerability of a healed woman. As the pandemic brought live music to a grinding halt in 2020, Levitin channeled her creative energies into music production and began shining a light on gender inequity in the music industry. Together with a team of talented DC creatives, she self-produced her debut LP, released on her 37th birthday, 3/21/2024. “I would describe [Levitin] as: If Brandi and Belinda Carlisle had a baby, and that baby was raised by the Mickey Mouse Club.” - Annie Stokes

rows.title: Paige Fish – The Midnight Crisis Tour
rows.description: Paige Fish, the Utah-born songstress from Springville, has captivated audiences with a voice and presence beyond her years. Drawing inspiration from the likes of Stevie Nicks, Norah Jones, Noah Kahan, and Zach Bryan, Paige has been songwriting since childhood, penning tunes and performing long before most artists get their start. She quickly found her footing on social media, capturing hearts and gaining a devoted following. In 2023, she released the standout track "26 and 24," which struck a chord with fans and marked a pivotal moment in her growing career. Since then, she has released three projects, including the fan-favorite "Baby Blondie". Paige has become a regular headliner, selling out shows across the country and building a passionate audience with her cinematic pop and country storytelling, which is rooted in deeply personal, diary-inspired lyrics.

rows.title: Unofficial Geese Afterparty w/ Seven Teller
rows.description: Seven Teller is the art-rock brainchild of Baltimore musician and songwriter Sam Cochran, who started the project in 2020. A blend of post-punk, dance, and psych-rock music nourishes the band’s unique sound. After several big releases and national tours, Seven Teller’s new full-length record What Are The Chances? will be available everywhere on 2/20/2026. Seven Teller is expanding the norms by creating music that’s reminiscent of acts like LCD Soundsystem, Talking Heads, and CAN, while still performing live shows that showcase deep improvisation, referencing their roots in the jam scene and early influences like Phish and Lotus. Seven Teller has featured sit-ins from Cotter Ellis (Goose), Jake Brownstein (Eggy), and Eli Winderman (Dopapod).

rows.title: Basia Bulat
rows.description: With an electrifying voice and lyrics like silver arrowheads, Basia Bulat has become one of Canada's most conspicuous talents. Juno nominated and short-listed for the prestigious Polaris Music Prize, she often appears solo in gigantic halls, winning over crowds with an autoharp or charango, stomping feet and two mighty lungs. Her massive talent has also been recognized at scale: her songs have been adapted for major performances with symphony orchestras, and she’s been tapped for prestigious tributes to Leonard Cohen and The Band. Since releasing her debut in 2007, she has shared a stage with artists including Arcade Fire, The National, Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, Daniel Lanois, St Vincent, Sufjan Stevens, Destroyer and Andrew Bird. Bulat was born in Toronto and grew up listening to her mother’s piano students, Sam Cooke and Stax on the oldies station. In early 2016 she released, Good Advice, produced by Jim James of My Morning Jacket.

Kennedy as he first arrived in Geor get own in 1946 as a 2 9-yea r-old congressman to his meteoric rise to our 35 th Presi dent. The t our is appropriate for all ages. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. This hike will utilize sidewalks that can be narrow and uneven at times. It will traverse nearly two miles of neighborhood streets in the Georgetown area of DC. The walk s tarts at the Georgetown Waterfront by Swedish Embassy on 30 th street.

rows.title: Introduction to Hiking: Woodland Loop with a Ranger
rows.description: During this ½ mile excursion, beginner explorers learn the hiking essentials, such as trail safety, what to wear or bring to a hike, and how to Recreate Responsibly all while looking at and respecting nature found in our woodlands. This ranger-led hike is intended to create treasured trail experiences for families interested in planning more advance hikes as their children become more experienced. Additional Information: This hike is recommended for families with children ages 5 and up. Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center porch, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

rows.title: Fun with Flora and Fauna
rows.description: Spend Friday afternoons and Sunday mornings at Rock Creek Park learning about our wild and wonderful urban oasis! Par k Rangers will teach kids (and people of all ages) about the fantastic flora and fauna in the park. Meet the ranger on the Nature Center front porch.

rows.title: Ranger Tours at Peirce Mill
rows.description: Step inside Peirce Mill, a rare surviving 19th-century gristmill in Rock Creek Park, and discover how waterpower once supported daily life in Washington, DC. Built in the 1820s, the mill served local farmers by grinding grain into flour and cornmeal. On this guided tour, you’ll explore the mill’s machinery, including the waterwheel, gears, and millstones that brought the process to life. Learn how the force of Rock Creek was harnessed to power the mill and the skill required to operate it. Rangers will share stories of the Peirce family and the workers who kept the mill running.

rows.title: Echoes of Time in Rock Creek Park Guided Hike
rows.description: The Milkhouse Ford trail offers both beautifully forested nature and a glimpse into Washington DC’s history. Ramble with a r anger for a guided hike on this 1.7-mile loop, where you will encounter 5000 years of history, from traces of Indigenous land usage, to Fort DeRussy (which saw action during the Civil War), to the two-room log cabin used by poet Joaquin Miller, and to the historic Milkhouse Ford river crossing (one of Rock Creek Park’s oldest and most well-preserved fords). Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing. For this Halloween hike, wear your costume!

rows.title: B.A.R.K. Ranger at Rock Creek Park
rows.description: Calling all dog owners! If you enjoy adventuring in Rock Creek Park with your furry friend, consider coming to one of our B.A.R.K. Ranger events! This is a national initiative to encourage responsible recreation and a positive experience for you, your dog, and all visitors to the park. Learn about the principles of being a B.A.R.K. Ranger and earn a B.A.R.K. Ranger badge! A ranger will be present to induct the new B.A.R.K. Rangers and distribute some fun doggie giveaways! A photo op will also be available to commemorate this great achievement! So how does one become a B.A.R.K. Ranger? By pledging to: B ag your pet’s waste A lways leash your pet R espect wildlife K now where you can go We hope you can bring your canine pals and join the fun! We encourage you to bring your pup in a Halloween costume!

rows.title: Ranger Tours at the Old Stone House
rows.description: Step back in time with a ranger-led tour of the Old Stone House, the oldest building in the nation’s capital. Discover what life was like in the 18th century as you explore its simple rooms, learn about early residents, and uncover the stories hidden within its stone walls. Perfect for visitors of all ages, this short tour offers a glimpse into everyday colonial life right in the heart of the city.

rows.title: Bike with a Ranger: Fall Leaves and Halloween Edition
rows.description: Join a ranger for an all-levels leisurely bike ride through Rock Creek Park to take in the fall colors and learn the science behind why the leaves change. Bring your own bike or get a Capital Bikeshare at Tilden St. and Connecticut Ave. NW (or other locations). Meet at Peirce Barn and b ring water and your curiosity for this 3.6-mile round trip ride. Come wearing your Halloween costume for this special edition of Bike with a Ranger! Don't forget your helmet!

rows.title: Ramble with a Ranger
rows.description: Join a ranger for a pleasant hike through the woods and along the creek. Ranger's choice of route - the hike may be between 1.5-3.5 miles. Come prepared with proper footwear and clothing, water, and curiosity to connect with nature. Meet on the front porch of the Nature Center and Planetarium.

rows.title: Roosevelt at Rock Creek Park
rows.description: Lace up your hiking boots and follow in the footsteps of Theodore Roosevelt, the adventurous president who believed that time spent in nature built character, courage, and a stronger nation. Beginning at Peirce Mill, this 1.5-mile (round-trip) guided hike winds through scenic trails and rugged landscapes that Roosevelt explored while escaping the pressures of the presidency. This hike covers uneven, tight, rocky terrain with steep elevation changes and may be challenging for some visitors. Participants should wear sturdy footwear, bring water, and dress appropriately for the weather. Recommended for ages 10 and older. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

rows.title: Fun with Flora and Fauna
rows.description: Spend Friday afternoons and Sunday mornings at Rock Creek Park learning about our wild and wonderful urban oasis! Par k Rangers will teach kids (and people of all ages) about the fantastic flora and fauna in the park. Meet the ranger on the front porch of the Nature Center.

rows.title: After Emancipation History Hike
rows.description: Step into a powerful and often untold chapter of local history on a 1.5-mile guided hike with a park ranger in the Peirce Mill area. Explore both the lives of formerly enslaved and contemporary individuals who built new beginnings in the community that became Rock Creek Park, discovering who they were, where they lived, and how their resilience and contributions helped shape the park we know today. Recommended for ages 12 and up. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm and be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.

rows.title: Ranger Tours at the Old Stone House
rows.description: Step back in time with a ranger-led tour of the Old Stone House, the oldest building in the nation’s capital. Discover what life was like in the 18th century as you explore its simple rooms, learn about early residents, and uncover the stories hidden within its stone walls. Perfect for visitors of all ages, this short tour offers a glimpse into everyday colonial life right in the heart of the city.

rows.title: Spilling the Tea at the Old Stone House
rows.description: From kitchen tables to acts of rebellion, tea fueled both daily life and political upheaval in colonial America. Visit the Old Stone House to sample historic teas and explore how this everyday drink became entangled in empire, protest, and revolution—earning its notorious reputation as the “baneful weed.”

rows.title: The Civil War in Georgetown: A Guided Walk in a City Divided
rows.description: Join a ranger on a walk to learn about Georgetown during one of the most turbulent chapters in American history. From the divided loyalties of Georgetown residents to the presence of Union soldiers, this tour reveals the hidden stories of a community caught between North and South. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. This hike will utilize sidewalks that can be narrow and uneven at times. It will traverse nearly two miles of neighborhood streets in the Georgetown area of DC. Additional Information: Tour departs from the Old Stone House There are no public facilities available on this hike. Recommended for ages 12 and up. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm. Or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm and be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.

rows.title: Mobilizing Memories at Meridian Hill
rows.description: Meridian Hill Park, colloquially referred to as Malcolm X Park, is known for its beauty, art, recreation, First Amendment space, and illustrious history. Join a ranger for a formal walking tour of the upper and lower terraces when you'll have the chance to visit the various statues and features of the park while exploring the theme of "who we choose to memorialize and why.” The tour meets by the bathrooms inside the park near 15 th Street and Euclid St. Please note: the walking tour involves going down several stairs. The walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm. Or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm and be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.

rows.title: Heroes Remembered: Stories from Battleground National Cemetery
rows.description: Join a ranger for a 30-minute, family-friendly walk through Battleground National Cemetery and discover the stories of the soldiers buried here. Learn who these men were and how their service helped shape our nation's history. Uncover clues about the lives of the soldiers, and think about how we remember people who served long ago. Through stories, questions, and observation, children and families will gain a deeper appreciation for the sacrifices made during one of the most important chapters in American history. Perfect for families with children ages 6 and up. This easy walking tour lasts approximately 30 minutes.

rows.title: Fall Leaves in Rock Creek Park Hike
rows.description: Have you ever wondered how the trees in our treasured forests put on such a brilliant display in the autumn? Now you can join a ranger on this 2-mile hike to take in the fall colors and learn the science behind the spectacular color change as you feel the seasons shifting around you. This route has a steep but manageable climb. Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center porch, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

rows.title: Junior Ranger Discovery Club: Explore, Learn, Protect
rows.description: Calling all future Junior Rangers! Get ready to travel back in time, uncover amazing stories, and discover what life was really like during the Civil War! At the Junior Ranger Discovery Club, every meeting is a new adventure. Collect Civil War trading cards, investigate what soldiers and families ate, discover what Civil War uniforms and equipment can tell us about the people who wore them, and try fun, hands-on activities that bring history to life. Complete challenges, ask questions, make discoveries, and learn how Junior Rangers can help protect the historic places and stories found in our national parks. Explore the past. Learn something new. Protect our parks. And have fun doing it! Recommended Ages: 8–12

rows.title: Books and Beyond with a Ranger at the Nature Center
rows.description: If you have a little one to take care of and are looking for something fun to do, come read and sing all about nature with a park ranger! This program includes nature books, animal puppets, body movements, and songs.

rows.title: Fort DeRussy Civil War Hike: Defending the Capital
rows.description: Join a ranger for a guided hike to Fort DeRussy, a Civil War site in Washington, DC. As you walk through the wooded landscape of Rock Creek Park, you’ll uncover how this fort helped protect the nation’s capital during a time of conflict. Along the way, learn about the soldiers who lived and worked here and the challenges they faced while stationed in the field. At the fort, explore the earthworks that still stand today and imagine what life was like inside this military post. Rangers will share stories of daily routines, military strategy, and the experiences of those who served here. This hike offers a chance to experience history where it happened while connecting with the natural landscape that surrounds it. This program begins at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center.

rows.title: Stitching Stories: A Social Stitch Circle at Peirce Mill
rows.description: Join Rock Creek Park's rangers for Stitching Stories, a community-powered knitting circle inspired by Freedom 250. Enjoy informal conversations about colonial-era fiber arts and how women used handmade textiles in daily life in support of the American Revolution. This is not a class—just a relaxed space for knitters of all levels to gather, chat, and work on their own projects. Bring a piece you’re already working on or start something new!

rows.title: Building Camelot: JFK in Georgetown
rows.description: Come join a ranger as we walk in the same path of John F. Kennedy as he first arrived in Geor get own in 1946 as a 2 9-yea r-old congressman to his meteoric rise to our 35 th Presi dent. The t our is appropriate for all ages. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. This hike will utilize sidewalks that can be narrow and uneven at times. It will traverse nearly two miles of neighborhood streets in the Georgetown area of DC. The walk s tarts at the Georgetown Waterfront by Swedish Embassy on 30 th street.

rows.title: Be a Junior Naturalist Hike
rows.description: Do you want to connect with nature but you’re not sure how to get started? Do you want to be more present outside and escape the distractions of the modern era? Take a junior naturalist hike with a ranger and learn how to observe and study the natural world around you as you hike between ½ - 1 ½ miles through the Rock Creek Valley. Come prepared with water, appropriate layers, comfortable hiking shoes, and an open mind willing to practice a new skill. Recommended ages 8+. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm. Be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.

rows.title: Fun with Flora and Fauna
rows.description: Spend Friday afternoons and Sunday mornings at Rock Creek Park learning about our wild and wonderful urban oasis! Par k Rangers will teach kids (and people of all ages) about the fantastic flora and fauna in the park. Meet the ranger on the Nature Center front porch.

rows.title: Stories in Stone: Monuments at Battleground National Cemetery
rows.description: Join a National Park Service ranger for a guided walk-through Battleground National Cemetery to explore Civil War monuments, their symbols, and the stories they were built to preserve. Discover how art, memory, and history come together in this quiet landscape where Washington, DC’s past is written in stone. As a part of the Freedom 250 commemoration, this program invites visitors to reflect on sacrifice, citizenship, and the enduring power of public memory. Please note that parking is limited to public streets.

rows.title: Friends of Georgetown Waterfront Park Labyrinth Program
rows.description: Please join us for a guided walk of the labyrinth in the Georgetown Waterfront Park. The labyrinth is a calming place for tourists, residents and visitors of all types to connect with nature, themselves and each other, all amidst the bustle of urban Washington, DC. This free event is coordinated by the Friends of Georgetown Waterfront Park.

rows.title: Ranger Tours at the Old Stone House
rows.description: Step back in time with a ranger-led tour of the Old Stone House, the oldest building in the nation’s capital. Discover what life was like in the 18th century as you explore its simple rooms, learn about early residents, and uncover the stories hidden within its stone walls. Perfect for visitors of all ages, this short tour offers a glimpse into everyday colonial life right in the heart of the city.

rows.title: Heroes Remembered: Stories from Battleground National Cemetery

Through stories, questions, and observation, children and families will gain a deeper appreciation for the sacrifices made during one of the most important chapters in American history. Perfect for families with children ages 6 and up. This easy walking tour lasts approximately 30 minutes.

rows.title: Ramble with a Ranger
rows.description: Join a ranger for a pleasant hike through the woods and along the creek. Ranger's choice of route - the hike may be between 1.5-3.5 miles. Come prepared with proper footwear and clothing, water, and curiosity to connect with nature. Meet on the front porch of the Nature Center and Planetarium.

rows.description: Have you ever wondered how the trees in our treasured forests put on such a brilliant display in the autumn? Now you can join a ranger on this 2-mile hike to take in the fall colors and learn the science behind the spectacular color change as you feel the seasons shifting around you. This route has a steep but manageable climb. Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center porch, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

rows.title: Roosevelt at Rock Creek Park
rows.description: Lace up your hiking boots and follow in the footsteps of Theodore Roosevelt, the adventurous president who believed that time spent in nature built character, courage, and a stronger nation. Beginning at Peirce Mill, this 1.5-mile (round-trip) guided hike winds through scenic trails and rugged landscapes that Roosevelt explored while escaping the pressures of the presidency. This hike covers uneven, tight, rocky terrain with steep elevation changes and may be challenging for some visitors. Participants should wear sturdy footwear, bring water, and dress appropriately for the weather. Recommended for ages 10 and older. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

rows.title: The Art of Landscape: Beatrix Farrand's Enduring Imprint on Dumbarton Oaks
rows.description: Beatrix Farrand is considered the first commercially successful woman landscape architect in the United States. Dumbarton Oaks Park in Georgetown is one of her lasting legacies. Come explore her creation with park rangers and learn how her design philosophy and unique vision helped shape this landscape, how that vision was nearly lost, and how the NPS and Dumbarton Oaks Park Conservancy are working to see that vision reimplemented today. Meet at the Dumbarton Oaks Park sign on R St. NW between 31 st St. NW and Avon Pl. NW. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. Feel free to check the Rock Creek Park website the day of to confirm. Or call the Nature Center (202-895-6070) the day of to confirm and be sure to leave a voicemail for a callback.

rows.title: Harbour
rows.description: Since their formation in 2014, HARBOUR has gone from packing rooms in their native Cincinnati to selling out venues across the United States. Members Ryan Green (vocals/guitar), Jarett Lewis (guitar), Devon Turner (guitar), and Ryan Sulken (drums) have curated an infectious, high energy sound that transfers seamlessly into their live shows. During their tenure as a group, HARBOUR has delivered 5 full length albums - the latest of which, entitled Great, Big, Insignificant, was released in October, 2025 after much anticipation. After supporting artists such as Bilmuri & Wilderado, HARBOUR successfully completed their first multinational headline tour in 2025. With more shows on the way in celebration of the new album, and even more music in the works, the band's future is sure to be anything but insignificant.

rows.title: Madds Buckley
rows.description: In an increasingly artificial world, singer-songwriter Madds Buckley is staying undeniably human. An RIAA Gold-certified artist with more than 2 million monthly listeners, Buckley pairs clear vocals with unexpected melodies and a deep-rooted instinct for storytelling. Her music sits at a unique intersection: honest, accessible, and highly personal storytelling that often incorporates themes found in anime, video games, and narrative-driven media. Even at its most fantastical, her music never loses sight of what’s real. Following My Love Is Sick, Buckley continues to evolve with a new run of releases, including “Overboard,” “Concept Without Proof,” and “Human to You,” ahead of her forthcoming album Simple Binary and a Complex Phrase (out October 16). Expanding her sonic and thematic scope more than ever before, the album interrogates the artificial to get to the heart of what’s most real: loving, losing, and persevering through the pain. Madds Buckley has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 per ticket goes to supporting Conscious Alliance’s mission to end hunger nationwide and feed families in need.

rows.title: Rainao: Marcriá tour
rows.description: Presale starts August 11th at 10am EST! Puerto Rican artist, saxophonist & composer, RaiNao, is one of Puerto Rico’s most exciting rising stars who boast 7M monthly listeners on Spotify. Born and raised in the vibrant Santurce neighborhood, at a young age her father, a passionate musician, instilled in her a love for music. After studying saxophone at the Libre de Música school her musical journey and knowledge led her to enthrall listeners with her experimental sound which blends genres such as hyperpop, reggaeton, R&B, guajira & others. 2025 was a career defining year for RaiNao. She scored her first No. 1 on Billboard alongside Bad Bunny for their song “PERFUMITO NUEVO” which they debuted on Saturday Night Live, was invited to walk the runway at Willy Chavarria’s show during Paris Fashion Week, received a Premios Juventud nomination under the category Girl Power and performed at Bad Bunny’s entire residency in Puerto Rico. 2026 kicked off with 2 Premio Lo Nuestro nominations under the categories Breakthrough Female Artist & Collaboration of the Year – Urban, further cementing her as one of the most impactful voices of her generation. In 2024, she released her album, CAPICÚ, which garnered heavy buzz and praise from top tier media. The album made it to several Best of 2024 lists including: Rolling Stone’s Best Albums of 2024 So Far, NPR’s Best Songs of 2024, Rolling Stone’s The Best Latin Albums of 2024, Rolling Stone en Español’s Best 50 Songs of 2024, & Latina’s Top 20 Songs of 2024. Her unapologetic attitude and fearless style have led her to collaborate with artists like Bad Bunny, Tainy, Villano Antillano, Álvaro Díaz, De la Ghetto & Mora, amongst others. In 2024, she also had her biggest show to date in San Juan, PR where she performed at a historic venue with 4K fans in attendance. In addition, she performed at the first ever concert at the iconic Louvre in Paris and was the only Latina invited to perform.

rows.title: Silly Goose – The “Set It Off” Tour
rows.description: Never content to sit still on the sidelines, Silly Goose slip through styles with a slick swagger. They’re salty enough to bust out a rap-rock banger that could just as easily light up the phones at TRL back in the day or the pit at Sonic Temple next year. At the same time, their emotionally charged melodies are smooth enough to get stuck in your head and stay there. Boasting an intoxicating blend of heavy metal, hip-hop, and alternative, they might steal your girl on one track, escape from prehistoric predators on another, or slyly address society’s struggles on the next. Stacking millions of streams, earning widespread acclaim, and packing houses on tour, the group—Jackson Foster [vocals], Alan Benikhis [drums], and Ian Binion [guitar]—consistently flip the script without apology on their second full-length LP and Blue Grape Music debut, Keys To The City. “The music goes in directions you might not expect,” promises Jackson. “There’s the lighthearted party vibe that Silly Goose is sort of known for. However, there are new elements. The songs get heavier, and it’s a little angrier too. For me, a track can be serious or crazy, but the subject matter will always be cohesive. We want you to be able to tell what every song is about and know exactly what we’re saying.”

performers.name: Silly Goose – The “Set It Off” Tour

rows.title: Cem Adrian
rows.description: One of the most distinctive singer-songwriters to emerge from Turkey in the last two decades, Cem Adrian has built a career defined by fearless experimentation and emotional depth. Blending alternative pop, folk, jazz, classical influences, he is creating a sound that is both intimate and expansive. Known for his extraordinary vocal range and haunting performances, Adrian has become one of Turkey’s most respected singer-songwriters, earning a devoted following through his uncompromising artistic vision rather than mainstream conventions. Since the release of his debut album Ben Bu Şarkıyı Sana Yazdım in 2005, Cem Adrian has continuously pushed the boundaries of Turkish music, releasing an extensive catalog that explores themes of love, loss, identity, solitude, and resilience. Whether performing stripped-back piano ballads or cinematic orchestral compositions, Adrian’s music is distinguished by its emotional honesty and poetic lyricism. Over two decades into his career, Cem Adrian remains one of the defining figures of Turkey’s independent music scene. His concerts are renowned for their intimacy and emotional intensity, transforming each performance into a deeply personal experience that resonates with audiences long after the final note. Constantly evolving while staying true to his artistic voice, Cem Adrian continues to inspire listeners with music that transcends genres, generations, and borders. Songs such as “Kül,” “Ben Seni Çok Sevdim,” “Herkes Gider Mi?,” “Sen Gel Diyorsun,”and“Derinlerde” have amassed millions of streams while showcasing his signature blend of poetic lyricism, haunting melodies, and emotionally charged performances. Continuously evolving without compromising his artistic vision, Adrian remains a defining voice in Turkish music, connecting with audiences through songs that are both deeply personal and universally resonant.

rows.title: Q Marsden - DO YOU SEE ME?
rows.description: Presale begins August 19th 10:00 AM EST! Union Stage Presents Presale begins August 20th 10:00 AM EST Q doesn’t just make music. He lives with it. He trusts it. He respects it. He breathes it. He gives his all to it. When you press play, you’re not only hearing his voice, his proficiency across multiple instruments, and his production acumen, but you’re also hearing his soul, spirit, and life amplified aloud. This intimacy has bonded the Florida-born singer, songwriter, and producer to a growing fanbase worldwide. He forged his own relationship with music as a kid in Miramar, FL. Born to musician parents, he cut his first track at just five-years-old. With a voracious appetite to create, he taught himself piano, guitar, bass, drums, and keys. Honing his craft over the years, he learned the ins and outs of production. He served up fan favorite releases such as Thoughts [2018], Forest Green [2019], The Shave Experiment EP [2020], The Shave Experiment (Director’s Cut) [2021], and Soul,PRESENT [2023]—hailed by NPR as “a collection of soulful songs steeped in analog nostalgia and & 80s pop production, with an eye toward a slightly more warped and wondrous future.” Simultaneously he clocked over half-a-billion streams fueled by the likes of “Garage Rooftop,” “TODAY,” and the breakout “Take Me Where Your Heart Is,” which generated north of 241 million streams. Along the way, he incited widespread tastemaker praise from The New York Times, Complex, Hypebeast, Noisey, Teen Vogue, Billboard, and PAPER who raved, “He exudes a natural X factor and effortless musical talent that harkens back to a bygone era of soul-pop acts like Stevie Wonder and Prince.” However, his relationship with music is forever. Never stopping, he picks up the pace again in 2025 with 10 songs [Columbia Records] and more to come.

performers.name: Q Marsden - DO YOU SEE ME?

rows.title: Carsie Blanton
rows.description: Carsie Blanton Carsie Blanton is a songwriter with hooks, chutzpah, and revolutionary optimism. A radical folk artist in the tradition of Woody Guthrie, her infectious melodies and lyrical wit keep listeners rapt while she conjures spirits of vaudeville, campfire singalongs, and punk rock. Blanton and her road-tested band deploy humor, camaraderie, and considerable musical muscle to enroll each audience in a rare vision of hope and solidarity. In addition to writing and performing music, Carsie works as a political organizer and activist. In fall of 2025, she participated in the Global Sumud Flotilla, a direct action to bring humanitarian aid to Gaza by sailboat. In early October, after a month at sea, she was imprisoned in Israel for five days along with hundreds of her comrades. Soon after, Blanton released The Little Flame, a song of solidarity covered widely on social media during her detention. The Little Flame features background vocals from Irish band Ye Vagabonds and Carsie’s Palestinian/New Zealander prison-mate Rana Hamida, and appears on her latest album, The Red Album Vol II. After two decades spent on the road, Blanton has amassed a dedicated fan base and a small menagerie of viral hits, and regularly sells out mid-size venues across the U.S. and Europe. 2026 will find her touring heavily with her own band and in collaboration with Canadian folk-punk rabblerousers The Burning Hell, as well as continuing her organizing work with Artists Against Apartheid, Party for Socialism and Liberation and others.

A limited number of binoculars are available for loan with a photo ID. The walk will be conducted at a leisurely pace, covering approximately one mile. We look forward to sharing this delightful experience with you!

books.title: Moss'd in Space
books.description:
Torian Razner finally bought a starship, and contrary to Amelia’s assessment, it was not “a meteoric sign of stupidity.” Sure, the alien starship may have been abandoned for a century, and it may be covered in moss now… but it’s Torian’s ticket to freedom, regardless of what her ex… ah, captain… said.

Except Torian’s first flight reveals a surprise passenger: the moss is actually an organic computer with a snarky attitude and serious abandonment issues. The target of its loathing? The immortal alien who built it (and then parked the starship, with Moss inside, and forgot about it). The same alien who just found Torian and accused her of “stealing” the ship.

It’s entirely possible that Amelia was right about this meteoric stupidity.

rows.title: The Smithereens featuring John Cowsill
rows.description: Founded in New Jersey in 1980, The Smithereens have been creating electrifying, original rock’n’roll for44 years.Jim Babjak (guitar,) Dennis Diken (drums,) and Mike Mesaros (bass) grew up together inCarteret and lead singer, the late Pat DiNizio,hailed from Scotch Plains. The band paid its dues in clubsall over the NYC tri-state area from Kenny’s Castaways in Greenwich Village to the Court Tavern andStone Pony in NJ. They’ve since performed on stages coast to coast from the Greek Theatre in LosAngeles to the Meadowlands Arena in NJ to Radio City Music Hall in Manhattan, and internationally fromEurope to Australia. Tour mates have included Tom Petty, Squeeze, The Pretenders, Lou Reed, and theRamones, among others.The Smithereens’ take no prisoners sound, reflecting their Garden State roots, has resonated with fansworldwide over the course of 17 albums and 2500 plus live shows. Studio albums include Especially forYou, Green Thoughts, 11, A Date with The Smithereens, and 2011. Among their biggest hits are the rockradio staples “Blood and Roses,” “Only a Memory,” “Behind the Wall of Sleep,” and “A Girl Like You.” Theband’s albums for Capitol, RCA, Sony, Koch, and eOne Records have sold over 5 million copiesworldwide.The Smithereens have alsobeen called the architects of theAlternativeScene and their music hasinspired and influenced generations of musicians, including the late Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, who citedThe Smithereens as a major influence in his diaries. You must be 18 or over to enter unless accompanied by your parent. Valid ID required. Save some money! There's only a $1 fee when you buy your ticket in person at the box office.

books.title: Au bonheur des dames
books.description: Translated into English titled "The Ladies Paradise". BBC did a series  on Masterpiece Theater.The novel tells the story of Denise Baudu, a 20-year-old woman who comes to Paris with her younger brothers and begins working as a saleswoman at the department store Au Bonheur des Dames. You read about the inner workings of the store from the employees' perspective, including the 13-hour workdays, and the bare lodgings for the female staff. Many of the conflicts in the novel spring from each employee's struggle for advancement and the malicious infighting and gossip among the staff.Denise's story is played against the career of Octave Mouret, the owner of Au Bonheur des Dames, whose retail innovations and store expansions threaten the existence of all the neighborhood shops. There's also a love story.

rows.title: An Evening with Mike Dawes
rows.description: This show is part of the Jammin Java/Union Stage Presents 25th anniversary concert series! Join us in celebrating 25 years, and check out our commemorative merch at the Union Stage Presents 25th anniversary Gift Shop! Mike Dawes “HE’S ONE OF THE FINEST I’VE EVER HEARD” – Rick Beato Mike Dawes is an English guitarist known for composing, arranging, and performing multiple parts simultaneously on a single guitar. He is regarded as one of the world’s most creative modern fingerstyle guitarists, with a repertoire spanning original viral videos and popular arrangements, alongside mainstream chart success performing with Justin Hayward of The Moody Blues. Dawes was named ‘Best Acoustic Guitarist in the World’ two years in a row (2017 & 2018) by Total Guitar Magazine & MusicRadar reader polls, with numerous 2nd place rankings in the proceeding years. YouTube personality Rick Beato named Mike ‘one of the finest acoustic guitar players in the world.’ His debut release, a solo guitar arrangement of Gotye’s ‘Somebody That I Used to Know,’ quickly became a viral hit with tens of millions of views on YouTube. This success has been duplicated and expanded upon numerous times since with songs like ‘One,’ ‘The Impossible,’ and ‘Jump’ across multiple video platforms. His reputation has invited him opportunities to collaborate with GRAMMY Award-winning artists such as Tommy Emmanuel, with whom he recorded the duet record ‘Accomplice Vol. 3,’ and the GRAMMY-nominated metal band Periphery, with whom Mike joined on their 2024 double single release.Mike is featured on multiple Justin Hayward live releases, including Spirits…Live, which debuted at #2 on the US Billboard Chart. Dawes also has a strong reputation as an educator, acting as a columnist for Guitar World and Acoustic Guitar magazines, as well as teaching guitar masterclasses all over the world, creating apps, publishing degree-level literature, appearing as a TV judge on SKY TV’s ‘Guitar Star,’ and more. Recently, he contributed electric guitars to Mentrix and Gareth Croker’s stunning soundtrack to Ubisoft’s Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown, with other session work featured on TV shows such as AMC’s Better Call Saul. Mike’s passion, however, is performing. He has shared the stage with acts as diverse as Tommy Emmanuel, Christopher Cross, Periphery, The Aristocrats, Justin Hayward, and the Athens State Orchestra in 2023 alone. His third studio album, Galactic Acid, is anticipated for release in August 2024.

rows.title: The Speaks + Crash Boom Bang: Spooky Halloween Party!
rows.description: From 1997 to 2009, The Speaks were known for 3 things: great anthemic music, amazing live shows, and drinking copious amounts of alcohol. From their radio debut on DC101 in 2003 to their 5th sell out show at the 9:30 club for their finale, The Speaks, who's members are of Filipino heritage, broke down barriers and were able to reach fans from all over the globe. In 2005, The Speaks signed a deal with Warner Music (Asia) with the "Life's a Joke" album release in the Philippines. The second single of the album, "High" received an unprecedented amount of worldwide airplay and is still being covered today from artists all over the world on YouTube. The Speaks released their final EP, "This is the Time" in 2008 and was distributed by Universal Music (Asia). From sharing the stage with national acts, to having their music videos receive heavy rotation on MTV Asia and MYX Music Channel, and still to this day being streamed over 1 million times monthly, The Speaks left their mark on the music scene and plenty of hangovers all over the world. Crash Boom Bang returns to the stage in 2026 after nearly a decade away, reuniting the band that helped define a chapter of the Washington DC pop-rock scene. Known for selling out hometown shows and bringing an explosive energy to every room, the band first broke out in the early 2010s, cutting their teeth at Jammin Java—where they packed the house show after show and built a loyal local following. Their momentum took them from Virginia to the national stage, touring alongside acts like Plain White T’s, Mayday Parade and Gin Blossoms. In 2012, the band released These Wild Things, an EP whose songs found placements in films and television including American Pie and Beauty and the Beast. Their high-octane music video for “V.I.P.” sparked online buzz and surpassed 300,000 views, expanding their audience far beyond the DMV. It was the perfect follwo-up to their debut album Gold Rush, which set the tone for their signature blend of anthemic pop-rock and high-energy hooks, produced by Plain White T's lead singer Tom Higgenson of "Hey There Delilah" fame. After their last major show in 2014, life pulled the guys in different directions—but the music never stopped calling. Now, Crash Boom Bang returns to Jammin Java, the venue where it all began, for one night only. Expect the same electric energy, sing-along hooks, and unapologetic fun that made their early shows legendary. This reunion marks a long-awaited celebration of where they came from—and the soundtrack of everyone who was there along the way. This show is part of the Jammin Java/Union Stage Presents 25th anniversary concert series! Join us in celebrating 25 years, and check out our commemorative merch at the Union Stage Presents 25th anniversary Gift Shop! After 8 years of performing together as Wandering Lies, a female fronted band from Washington, D.C., the Angie Pepa fronted rock band has decided to rebrand and go in a new musical direction with a new project called " Kill For Sushi ". As Wandering Lies, Pepa and her bandmates (guitarist Noli Conty, bassist Myk Menez, guitarist David Chaletzky, drummer Ben Tufts) won 4 battle of the bands, were nominated as best rock group in 2021 by the Washington Area Music Association, and were a finalist to open up the iHeartRadio Festival by Hot 99.5 in 2020. The band is working on a new album that will be released in 2026.

rows.title: The Nth Power
rows.description: The Nth Power believes in the healing power of music. Featuring guitarist Nick Cassarino, bassist Nate Edgar and drummer Nikki Glaspie, the seasoned trio delivers a transcendent blend of soul, funk, rock and rhythm and blues. Multi-part vocal harmonies and elevated musicianship inspires audiences to dance, groove, make love or just stand there with goose bumps. The Nth Power’s electric live performances have been flooring audiences ever since the group first aligned in New Orleans during Jazz Fest. After the band’s breakout 2013 EP, Basic Minimum Skills Test, The Nth Power went on to release two acclaimed studio albums and two live albums – garnering national coverage in Relix, Modern Drummer, Huffington Post, Glide, Consequence, Okayplayer, Paste and Sirius XM Radio. The trio’s individual music credentials include collaborating with artists like Beyonce, Snarky Puppy, Maceo Parker, Dumpstaphunk, Big Daddy Kane and John Brown's Body. “It’s my dream team,” said bandleader and drummer Glaspie. “Each one of us is a songwriter, so when we get together, everything becomes that much stronger. We’re going as far as you can go on the planet Earth and playing music.” The Nth Power's inspirational sets have floored audiences at music festivals like Electric Forest, High Sierra, Peachfest, North Coast Music Festival and Hulaween. They maintain New Orleans as their spiritual home, and the celebratory essence of that city’s music culture is palpable in each performance. Simply put, there is something pretty magical happening in this band, and they’re only just getting started.

rows.title: The Alternate Routes & Pete Muller & The Kindred Souls
rows.description: The Alternate Routes are the band that helped us to remember “we are how we treat each other, and nothing more.” “Nothing More” propelled the band into new ears and new heights, having been featured prominently in the 2014 Winter Olympics, on NCIS, and with numerous other organizations. It was followed up with “Somewhere in America,” a poignant and personal conversation about gun violence that earned the band a 2016 Independent Music Award and a visit to the White House. The Alternate Routes first burst onto the scene in 2005 with their breakthrough album Good and Reckless and True. They released several albums on Vanguard Records and on their own, toured extensively, and relentlessly refined their craft. They have collaborated with such seemingly disparate artists as singer-songwriter Patti Griffin, director Lisa Cholodenko (The Kids Are All Right), and guitarist Carl Broemel of My Morning Jacket. They’ve performed on The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson, Late Night with Conan O’Brien, and have been repeat guests on NPR’s Mountain Stage. Critically acclaimed songwriter and pianist Pete Muller is known for his dynamic live shows and genre-spanning blend of roots, rock, soul, and pop. His new album One Last Dance, was recorded at Peter Gabriel’s Real World Studios and features Grammy- winner Allison Russell and SistaStrings. Backed by his band, The Kindred Souls—Eric Donnelly (guitar), Martha McDonnell (violin), Skip Ward (bass), and Andy Mac (drums)—Muller delivers powerful, heartfelt performances that have earned him festival slots from Telluride to Montreux and dates with Jimmy Webb, Lisa Loeb, Livingston Taylor, and more. Onstage, Muller’s passion and chemistry shine, making every show unforgettable.

rows.title: Josh Rouse
rows.description: For fans of Kings of Convenience, Cat Power, and Pete Yorn Hailed by NPR as “one of contemporary music’s most engaging singer-songwriters, ” Josh Rouse first emerged with his stunning 1998 debut, Dressed Up Like Nebraska, which Billboard proclaimed a “dark horse gem. ” In the years to come, he would continue to refine his warm, ruminative sound, releasing thirteen more critically acclaimed albums, performing everywhere from Glastonbury to Massey Hall, and taking home a prestigious Goya Award (the Spanish equivalent of an Oscar) for his song "Do You Really Want To Be In Love. " His next record will be released by New West Records in the fall of 2026.

rows.title: Rock for Schools II - A benefit for Educate Fairfax
rows.description: For fans of Nuno Riberio, Soraia Ramos, and popping off to some of Portugal's hottest pop music! Rock for Schools II For the second year, three bands with teachers (The Pool Boys, The Aftermath, and The Randos) will rock Jammin' Java to benefit Educate Fairfax, a nonprofit that works with Fairfax County Public Schools to provide school supplies, scholarships, and grants for education innovations. The Pool Boys are a rock cover band from Herndon, Va., specializing in an eclectic mix of high-energy rock tunes (Red Hot Chili Peppers, Nirvana, Green Day, Rage Against the Machine), hip-hop party tunes (Eminem, Nelly, Dr. Dre, Run-DMC), and classic rock (Aerosmith, Tom Petty, the Doobie Brothers, Van Halen). Guitarist/vocalist Dan Blanchet is also the chair of the social studies department at Madison High School in Vienna. The Aftermath is a party pop rock band playing your favorites from the 80's to today from bands like Jimmy Eat World, Wheatus, No Doubt, Lit, Bon Jovi, and the Killers. Lead singer Molly Jepsen is a math teacher at Madison High School in Vienna. The Randos are a band from Vienna and Arlington featuring music from the glory days of MTV (The Cure, R.E.M., INXS, Men at Work) with a few surprises from before (CCR, Fleetwood Mac) and after (Neon Trees, Chris Stapleton) the days in which Music Television had music. Lead singer Kristy Woldow is a music teacher in Arlington; multi-instrumentalist Beau Dure is a substitute teacher in FCPS.

rows.title: Community Exhibit: Altar del Día de Los Muertos
rows.description: Across the Americas, people commemorate loved ones with offerings of their favorite foods, objects, and stories. This ceremony observes the interconnectedness of life and death, a natural cycle experienced by all forms of life. Through October 27th and November 3rd, Meadowside Nature Center welcomes offerings (“ofrenda”) in a community exhibit discussing cycles of rest and renewal, and cultural traditions that celebrate death as a universal experience. Registration is not required. Guests may come anytime during open hours to place copies of photographs, objects, flowers and plants, artwork, and non-perishable foods in sealed containers on the altar. The community exhibit will be open to the public; please provide objects that can be left at the nature center.

rows.title: Storytime: Collective Cafe at Maryland Hall
rows.description: Happy Halloween-calling all goblins and ghouls to our storytime! Join us for our traditional Halloween story, Creepy Pair of Underwear. Join us for the story, stay for the snack and family crafty craft. Be sure to RSVP on our website to enter to receive a free copy of our storytime book. Thank you to the Park Literacy Project for helping us spread the joy of reading by providing our book. About our book: Jasper Rabbit is NOT a little bunny anymore. He's not afraid of the dark, and he's definitely not afraid of something as silly as underwear. But when the lights go out, suddenly his new big rabbit underwear glows in the dark. A ghoulish, greenish glow. If Jasper didn't know any better he'd say his undies were a little, well, creepy. Jasper's not scared obviously, he's just done with creepy underwear. rows.description: Everts Foundation When you get a cancer diagnosis it immediately starts a journey for the whole family. Needless to say: It’s not a voyage anyone wants to go on. Fortunately, there are many organizations out there to help the patient get through the process. Many foundations send care packages with socks, water bottles, notebooks and more to the diagnosed. However, for the rest of the family there is a lack of these options, and it can feel as if they’re left to work out all the same emotions as their loved one, alone. That is where we come in. Our cause is to send care packages to families with items for everyone. Our hope is to help them get through the process together, so you never feel alone. https://evertsfoundation.org

rows.title: Arts on Stage Presents...A More Perfect Union
rows.description: Arts on Stage Presents… A More Perfect Union Wednesday, November 4, 2026 in the Hammonds Lane Theatre 10:15 am 12 pm $11.50 Grades 3-8 Study guide, click here A spirited folk musical introducing the people and events that led to the writing and signing of our Constitution. The story of “A More Perfect Union” begins in Boston, 1773 and ends at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia, 1787. The play covers the critical and tempestuous time in our nation’s history in which revolution, war, and a failed attempt at self-governing finally led to the writing of the U.S. Constitution and the birth of our country as we know it today. Briefly addressing the American Revolution and the underlying causes thereof, the majority of the play examines that period between the winning of our Independence and the formation of our national government.

rows.title: Park Literacy Project & Park Books of Maryland Presents.. Author Tini Younger
rows.description: Park Literacy Project & Park Books of Maryland Present…. Author Tini Younger November 4, 2026 5:30 pm | 6:30 pm Hammonds Lane Theatre Tickets: $35-$90 Park Literacy Project and our many partners welcome home one of our own. Tini Younger--Maryland native, trained chef, and the social media sensation behind some of the most-watched comfort food videos on the internet- is coming back to Maryland to celebrate the launch of her debut cookbook, Today We Are Cooking... Recipes That Teach You to Think Like a Chef! Join us for an evening with Tini as she prepares a delicious recipe live from the book, answers your questions, and proves that the best food always starts in your own kitchen when you think like a chef! Every attendee will leave with a signed copy of the cookbook! She may have taken her talents beyond the DMV, but a Baltimore girly never really leaves Raven's country! We could not be more excited to have her here! Let's get cookin'! This event is presented in partnership with Chesapeake Arts Center, Jimmy's Famous Seafood, and Park Books of Maryland. This event is brought to you by Park Literacy Project. Park Literacy Project LLC provides equitable access to books, literacy programming, and evidence-based reading instruction. By creating literacy-rich third spaces and providing scholarships, they empower Maryland families to discover the joy of reading regardless of zip code. Tini shares over 100 recipes that build a strong foundation for beginner cooks. With learning opportunities baked into every recipe, Tini teaches you why you are doing something rather than just how to do it, all with her casual, unfussy approach. Today We Are Cooking is packed with plenty of easy, everyday meals that you’llwant to cook time and time again. You’ll find OG favorites like Tini’s Viral Mac and Cheese and her favorite Banana Bread plus dozens of new, elevated comfort food recipes,all of which have a special Tini spin—like Oven-Cooked BBQ Pulled Pork with Spicy Slaw, Chicken Soup with Homemade Noodles, and Creamy Grits with Sautéed Mushrooms and Butternut Squash. Every recipe highlights the skills you’ll learn while making it and includes pro tips from Tini along with ideas for how to “own it” with swaps or twists to personalize the dish. Tini covers all the staples for breakfast, dinner, game days, and more—and there’s even a chapter of her most beloved holiday dishes. Getting in the kitchen changed Tini’s life, so she’s passionate about helping home cooksgain their own confidence in the kitchen. Today We Are Cooking will be your go-to resource for recipes that work every time. ABOUT THE AUTHOR: Tineke "Tini" Younger is a chef, bestselling digital creator, entrepreneur, and author redefining what it means to build a modern culinary brand. Widely recognized as one of the most influential food creators of her generation, Tini has transformed home cooking into a cultural phenomenon through her approachable recipes, authentic storytelling, and ability to build genuine community online. Her impact has earned her recognition as a Forbes Top Creator, a member of the prestigious TIME100 Creators List, inclusion on the Create & Cultivate 100 List, and selection to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Class of 2026.

rows.title: Morning Flag Change
rows.description: Fort McHenry holds a unique honor as the very first site to receive a presidential proclamation requiring the U.S. flag to fly 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Each day, you’re invited to join park staff for our morning and evening flag‑changing traditions. Discover why the flag became a powerful symbol during the Battle of Baltimore and how it became deeply tied to the nation’s story as the inspiration behind the Star-Spangled Banner. In the mornings, we raise a replica of a historic flag. In the evenings, we lift an all‑weather flag that proudly flies through the night. Don’t just read about history—experience it! Plan your visit, join a flag program, and be part of a tradition that connects us to the nation’s story. *Flag changes are weather dependent. More information

rows.title: 250 Years of Service: Armistice Day and the Origins of Veterans Day at Fort McHenry
rows.description: What did the Great War teach us? Honoring Service, Sacrifice and Preserving Peace. Established by President Wilson in 1919, Armistice Day encouraged commemoration of the end of the Great War, and community recognition of both service and sacrifice. This marked the first national remembrance of the armistice as the end of the war. Though the holiday was later renamed Veterans Day to recognize the service of all veterans (not solely those of World War I), its dual purpose remained true to its origins and, in the words of President Eisenhower, Americans would: “…solemnly remember the sacrifices of all those who fought so valiantly on the seas, in the air, and on foreign shores to preserve our heritage of freedom, and …reconsecrate ourselves to the task of promoting an enduring peace so that their efforts shall not have been in vain.” Through the weekend, visitors will explore the history of General Hospital No. 2 at Fort McHenry during World War I and be encouraged to consider the following questions: What challenges did those serving at General Hospital No. 2 face? How did the World War I generation remember the war? What did they want for the future? How can we best honor the service and sacrifice of current and past generations? rows.title: Ron White
rows.description: Renowned comedian Ron White, affectionately known as "Tater Salad," catapulted into the limelight as the cigar-wielding, scotch-savoring humorist who stole the spotlight within the Blue Collar Comedy Tour phenomenon. Yet, his trajectory has evolved into an extraordinary journey, one where he has risen to chart-topping Grammy-nominated comic and a captivating feature film actor. At his core, Ron White remains an exemplar of timeless storytelling. His narratives weave the fabric of his existence, spanning from his upbringing in a Texan hamlet to the reflections of his everyday encounters, ultimately culminating in his ascension as one of America's most celebrated comedians. The unrivaled resonance of his humor is evident in the fact that all four of his comedy albums not only scaled the Billboard Comedy Charts but also claimed the coveted #1 position. The echoes of his comedic prowess started resonating in 1986, when Ron White embarked on his comedy journey, rapidly establishing himself as an opening act for comedic legends like Sam Kinison and Jeff Foxworthy. As his brilliance matured, he seized the stage as a headliner in comedy clubs, leading to an invitation in 2000 that would define an era: to join the ranks of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour alongside Jeff Foxworthy, Bill Engvall, and Larry the Cable Guy. For over three years, this ensemble embarked on a triumphant odyssey, captivating audiences across 270 cities and amassing over $35 million in ticket sales. The crowning glory was the cinematic rendition, "Blue Collar Comedy Tour: The Movie," which premiered as the most-watched Comedy Central film, leaving an indelible mark on popular culture. In 2003, Ron White unleashed his breakthrough comedy opus, "Drunk In Public," soon followed by his inaugural one-hour television special, aptly titled "They Call Me Tater Salad." This comedic masterpiece not only shattered viewership records but also solidified its place in history as Comedy Central's most-watched Sunday program. Subsequently, the evolution continued with "You Can’t Fix Stupid," which commanded an audience of 4.5 million viewers, rendering it the third most-watched show in Comedy Central's history. The accompanying CD soared to the #1 rank on the Billboard Comedy Charts and initiated Ron White's journey to Grammy recognition. Diversifying his creative output, Ron White penned his debut literary endeavor, "Ron 'Tater Salad' White: I Had the Right to Remain Silent…But I Didn’t Have the Ability," swiftly ascending to the New York Times Best Seller List. Ron’s contributions aren’t confined to comedy alone; the world sees his remarkable generosity as he has championed the US military troops for more than two decades, founding the cherished annual charity event, "Ron White’s Comedy Salute to the Troops." This heartwarming endeavor funneled proceeds to the Armed Forces Foundation, a testament to Ron White's unwavering dedication. Transitioning seamlessly into the realm of cinema, Ron White gave unforgettable performances in films like "Horrible Bosses," "Sex and the City 2," and the acclaimed "Jayne Mansfield’s Car," in which his charismatic presence emanated. Moreover, his role as a co-Executive Producer in the lauded documentary "Bridegroom" showcased his commitment to meaningful storytelling that resonates beyond laughter. His resolute commitment to the craft brought him to the small screen, as he embarked on a remarkable journey in Cameron Crowe's Showtime series, "Roadies," delivering a standout portrayal that resonated with both audiences and critics alike. In a symphony of achievements, Ron White's trajectory from humble beginnings to the echelons of comedy and entertainment is nothing short of awe-inspiring. His narratives have not only tickled the world's funny bone but have also etched a profound legacy that transcends stages, screens, and generations.

rows.title: Fireside Collective
rows.description: A quintet who cheerfully disregard every kind of one-dimensional label that might be attached to their music, Fireside Collective has been on a roll since emerging seven years ago from the fertile roots music scene of Asheville, North Carolina. In quick order, the progressive bluegrass group released its debut album, won the 2016 Band Contest at MerleFest, earned an International Bluegrass Music Association Momentum Band of the Year nomination and embarked on an ambitious touring schedule that’s earned an enthusiastic reception from traditional bluegrass to wide-ranging, eclectic music festival audiences alike. Blending the characteristic interplay of bluegrass instrumentation and harmonies with strong original material and exuberant energy, Fireside Collective has drawn on folk, blues, funk and a wide variety of bluegrass sounds to create a distinctive body of work that’s all their own. Each member—Joe Cicero (guitar); Alex Genova (banjo); Jesse Iaquinto (mandolin); Tommy Maher (resonator guitar) and Carson White (upright bass)— brings a strong, original voice to his instrument, and the unique contributions of different lead and harmony vocalists complement the variety in the group’s many original songs. “Depending on where you come from and your experience with folk music, you may think we’re very traditional, or on the other hand, consider us a progressive act,” says Iaquinto. “We appreciate both ends of the spectrum and may lie on a different end on any given night.” But whether they’re bringing the classic sound of bluegrass or exploring new musical territory, Fireside Collective delivers a fresh, energetic approach and a blast of enthusiastic creativity that’s electrifying audiences across the country.

rows.title: Collegiate World Premiere of The Musical, "Kenya's Soul"
rows.description: From the same group that brought "Aida," "The Color Purple," Dreamgirls," "Once on This Island," and "Echoes of Motown," comes the Collegiate World Premiere of the "Kenya's Soul" Morgan State University Musical Theatre is back to present this compelling, multi-faceted musical -- written and directed by Dr. Tyrone Stanley. In a world where wealth, image, and expectation define everyone’s role, Kenya Mugabo seems to have it all—status, privilege, and a future shaped by her family’s real estate empire. But as secrets about her birth mother emerge, Kenya’s polished life starts to unravel, forcing her to question who she really is. Her journey carries her across continents, from Manhattan’s glittering society to the ancestral heartbeat of Africa, where betrayal, inherited trauma, and painful revelations come to the surface. As Kenya uncovers her mother’s legacy, she also realizes she’s carrying a truth of her own—one that could shatter her family’s carefully built empire. With loyalty and legacy colliding, Kenya must choose whether protecting the empire means silencing her own soul. Ultimately, she discovers her voice and learns that true royalty isn’t inherited—it’s awakened. Experience the talent of MSU Musical Theatre and its ability to tell Kenya's story while showcasing a musical score that includes, romantic melodies, gritty, urban rhythms and World Music showstoppers. This production refers to, and addresses, mature themes. Parental discretion is advised. Tickets can be purchased in-person at the Murphy Fine Arts Center Ticket Office (open Wed-Fri, 1PM-4PM and Sat, 11AM-4PM). Tickets are $40 Reserved Seating. Discounts available for Seniors, Students and Groups.

rows.title: Mansion Tour
rows.description: The only way to see the interior of the mansion is by being on a mansion tour, with a ticket. Tours of the mansion offer a glimpse of over 150 years of American history as lived by the Ridgely family, European indentured servants, enslaved African Americans, and paid laborers. Visitors can join a guide and walk the halls of this historic structure and learn about its architectural features, artwork, and the thousands of other authentic collection items that are on display. The mansion's artifacts and decor is changed twice a year - once in the winter and again in the summer to showcase seasonal fashions and adjustments that predate modern utilities and luxuries. The only way to go inside the mansion is on a tour, with tickets! More information This event is free to attend. Tickets Required: Due to limited space on mansion tours, visitors must first get tickets for the tour. Tours are limited to 15 visitors a tour. Tickets are free and available on a first come, first serve basis at the park visitor center. Tickets can only be acquired the day of your visit. Tickets tend to go fast, so visitors are encouraged to get to the park early if they are interested in a mansion tour. Meet guide at ramp behind mansion. Latitude and Longitude 39.416370, -76.587426 Tours run approximately 45-60 minutes.

rows.title: Sophia Bush
rows.description: Sophia Bush has always understood the power of stories. She’s seen it in the connection millions of viewers have had to the women she’s played on-screen—Dr. Sam Griffith on “Good Sam” and Dr. Cass Beckman on “Grey’s Anatomy,” Detective Erin Lindsay on “Chicago P.D.,” and the iconic Brooke Davis on “One Tree Hill.” She’s seen it in her activism, where speaking truth to inequality and power has prompted real change. And she’s seen it in her personal life, when her experiences and opinions have been distorted to drive clicks and create drama. In And I Will Tell You Mine, Bush shares stories about what has most shaped her: her childhood in Los Angeles, the unexpected road from journalism student to actor, navigating Hollywood and fighting for her character’s integrity, and the realities of marriage and divorce. She also offers sides of herself not often seen: the lifelong learner, the friend, the adventurer. And I Will Tell You Mine is an account of becoming, un-becoming, and becoming again to return home to our truest selves. Bush will be in conversation with Aaron Parnas, an independent journalist, political commentator, and attorney. This service will be ASL-interpreted. To sit in the interpreted section or to access the interpreted feed virtually, contact Amanda.

rows.description: THEATRE DRAMA THE TRUMPETER Get Tickets Presented by: Alliance for New Music-Theatre in partnership with Ukraine House and United Help Ukraine Written by Inna Goncharova | English Translation by John Farndon Directed by János Szász Alliance for New Music-Theatre’s production of The Trumpeter returns to Dupont Underground for an immersive experience! Following a successful run garnering critical acclaim and a Helen Hayes Recommendation, this powerful production returns to the bunker-like tunnels of Dupont Underground for 13 performances. Staged in the tunnel, Inna Goncharova’s play captures the siege and bombing of Mariupol during the first year of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Directed by Hungarian director János Szász, the show features DC actors Michael Kevin Darnall and Lise Bruneau, enriched by trumpeter Kevin McKee and a male chorus of Ukrainian singers led by Ruslan Bondar. Audiences will also experience complementary photo exhibits curated by Ukraine House and United Help Ukraine in the venue prior to the performance. rows.title: Desi Alexander
rows.description: Baltimore native Desi Alexander is a high-energy stand-up comedian, writer, and director known for his fearless storytelling and razor-sharp wit. What started as teaching by day and performing by night quickly turned into a full-time calling — a destiny foreshadowed by the name his late father gave him, inspired by a classic bit from Eddie Murphy’s Delirious. With an engaged following of more than 500,000 fans worldwide, Desi has built a loyal audience drawn to his raw honesty, animated delivery, and relatable edge. His upcoming comedy special Stress Signal expands on the high-energy style that’s made him a crowd favorite across the country. Beyond the stage, Desi is the creative force behind Redeye Valley Films. His action film Flood is streaming on Tubi, while his acclaimed projects The Realtor (Amazon) and Check Please (Tubi) showcase his range as a writer and director. rows.title: An Afternoon with Rachel Levitin
rows.description: Imagine this - it’s Sunday afternoon and there’s nowhere you have to be. All that’s left is to sit back, relax, and decompress; leaving the heaviness of the modern world behind. Instead, you opt for a brief retreat to a sweet, experiential solace that is the matinee showing of a revered life-long artist’s latest creative connection with her audience. Join this interactive, conversational, live music concert curated and performed by singer-songwriter and executive producer Rachel Levitin. Hosted and guided by award-winning vocalist Jarreau Williams. “An Afternoon with Rachel Levitin” is a milestone event celebrating a wide variety of Rachel’s accomplishments such as: 30 years as a student of music, 27 as a songwriter, 21 since the release of her debut album “Come As You Are,” 20 living in the District of Columbia, 10 since the release of her unanimous fan-favorite “Get Back Up,” and 6 since production began on her 2024 album “Witty Banter,” all culminating to the world premiere of Rachel’s newest song, “Eulogy,” written, recorded, and performed in loving memory of her late grandfather, the beloved Edwin H. Levitin, who passed away in February 2026. Growing up in the city of Chicago, she didn't initially aspire to be a pop-rock recording artist, but an eclectic love of jazz, early aughts radio hits, and expressive ambition led Rachel Levitin to pick up her first guitar as a tween. As the ordinary and extraordinary traumas of early adulthood crashed down, Levitin channeled her grief, optimism, and growth into her lyrics. A move to DC in 2005 introduced her to the Washington-area music scene, where she quickly established a reputation for herself as a confident performer and a stalwart supporter of her peers. Her debut EP, "Nearly Broken" was released in 2015 and was followed by a string of singles, including 2021's "Off My Mind", which showcased Levitin's ability to write an unforgettable hook. In an age when wispy cynicism is en vogue, Levitin's earnest, raw lyricism sets her apart from the crowd. Her music combines the endorphin rushes of early aughts hits with the emotional vulnerability of a healed woman. As the pandemic brought live music to a grinding halt in 2020, Levitin channeled her creative energies into music production and began shining a light on gender inequity in the music industry. Together with a team of talented DC creatives, she self-produced her debut LP, released on her 37th birthday, 3/21/2024. “I would describe [Levitin] as: If Brandi and Belinda Carlisle had a baby, and that baby was raised by the Mickey Mouse Club.” - Annie Stokes
